source_text: 8.1. Et quoniam ridere nostram fidem consuestis atque ipsam credulitatem facctis iocularibus lancinare, dicite, o festivi et meraco sapientiae tincti et saturi potu, estne operis in vita negotiosum aliquod atque actuosum genus, quod non fide praeeunte suscipiant sumant atque adgrediantur actores? 2. Peregrinamini, navigatis non domum vos credentes peractis negotiationibus remeaturos? Terram ferro scinditis atque oppletis seminum variètate non credentes vos frugem percepturos esse vicibus temporariis? 3. Coniugalia copulatis consortia non futura esse credentes casta et officiosi foederis in maritos? Liberorum susceptatis prolem non incolumem credentes fore et per gradus aetatis venturam senectutis ad metas? 4. Aegritudines corporum medicorum committitis manibus non credentes morbos posse mitigata asperitate leniri? Bella cum hostibus geritis non victoriam vos credentes proeliorum successionibus relaturos? 5. Veneramini deos et colitis non credentes illos esse et propitias aures vestris supplicationibus accommodare?
pass_a_gloss: You mock nostram fidem / credulitatem. Is any busy life-work undertaken without fide praeeunte? Travel/sail, sow, marry, raise children, physicians, war — all require credentes. You even venerate gods only credentes they exist and hear.
pass_b_english: And since you are accustomed to laugh at our faith and to slash at credulity itself with joking strokes, say, O merry ones dyed and filled with wisdom’s neat wine: is there any busy and active kind of work in life that actors take up, seize, and approach without faith going before? Do you travel and sail without believing you will return home when business is done? Do you split the earth with iron and fill it with variety of seeds without believing you will take fruit in the turns of seasons? Do you join marital partnerships without believing they will be chaste and of dutiful bond toward husbands? Do you take on the offspring of children without believing it will be safe and come through the grades of age to the bounds of old age? Do you commit the body’s illnesses to physicians’ hands without believing diseases can be eased when harshness is softened? Do you wage wars with enemies without believing you will bring back victory by the successions of battles? Do you reverence and cultivate the gods without believing they exist and turn favorable ears to your prayers?

choices.why: Veneramini deos… non credentes illos esse?
